question: Change the QueryData method signature in the Loki standalone datasource to accept a new streaming parameter: QueryData(ctx context.Context, req *backend.QueryDataRequest, stream bool) (*backend.QueryDataResponse, error). This affects Loki's query API compatibility.

direct_change.proposed_signature: func (d *Datasource) QueryData(ctx context.Context, req *backend.QueryDataRequest, stream bool) (*backend.QueryDataResponse, error)

impact_analysis.summary: This change breaks the backend.QueryDataHandler interface contract from the Grafana Plugin SDK and cascades through the entire Loki query pipeline. It is NOT a safe change without coordinated modifications across the SDK, the core Service, and all callers.

affected_files.reason: Direct target. The Datasource struct asserts `_ backend.QueryDataHandler = (*Datasource)(nil)` at line 15. Adding the `stream bool` parameter breaks this interface assertion — the Datasource would no longer satisfy backend.QueryDataHandler, causing a compile-time error.

The standalone datasource delegates to `d.Service.QueryData(ctx, req)` (line 31 of datasource.go). The Service.QueryData method (line 182) must also be updated to accept `stream bool`. Service also asserts `_ backend.QueryDataHandler = (*Service)(nil)` at line 44, which would break.
The healthcheck function calls `s.QueryData(ctx, &backend.QueryDataRequest{...})` at line 56. This call would need a third argument (e.g., `false`) to compile after the signature change.

Loki already has streaming support via the backend.StreamHandler interface (SubscribeStream, RunStream, PublishStream). The `stream bool` parameter overlaps with existing streaming infrastructure that uses WebSocket-based tail endpoints. This creates architectural confusion between two streaming mechanisms.
Uses `datasource.Manage("loki", NewDatasource, ...)` which expects the instance to satisfy backend.QueryDataHandler. The modified Datasource would no longer match.

Registers loki.Service via `loki.ProvideService(httpClientProvider, tracer)` at line 240. The Service is used as a core plugin backend, and the plugin system calls QueryData through the backend.QueryDataHandler interface. The signature mismatch would cause a compile-time failure.
Test that instantiates loki.ProvideService and relies on it satisfying the plugin interfaces.

The backend.QueryDataHandler interface is defined in the external grafana-plugin-sdk-go module. Changing the method signature in Loki alone is impossible — the SDK interface defines QueryData as (context.Context, *QueryDataRequest) -> (*QueryDataResponse, error). To add a `stream bool` parameter, either: (1) the SDK interface itself must change (affecting ALL Grafana datasource plugins), or (2) the streaming parameter must be passed via a different mechanism (e.g., request headers, context values, or the existing QueryDataRequest struct).

impact_analysis.root_cause_of_breakage: backend.QueryDataHandler is an interface from grafana-plugin-sdk-go that defines `QueryData(context.Context, *backend.QueryDataRequest) (*backend.QueryDataResponse, error)`. Both Datasource (standalone) and Service (core) assert they implement this interface via compile-time checks. Adding a `stream bool` parameter changes the method signature so it no longer matches the interface, causing compilation failures.

alternative_approaches.approach: Add stream flag to QueryDataRequest headers
alternative_approaches.description: Pass the streaming intent via `req.Headers["X-Loki-Stream"] = "true"`. This preserves interface compatibility and follows the existing pattern of using headers (like `FromAlert`).
Use `context.WithValue(ctx, lokiStreamKey, true)` to pass the parameter without changing the signature. Similar to how feature flags are already passed via context.

alternative_approaches.approach: Embed stream flag in query JSON model
alternative_approaches.description: Add a `Stream bool` field to QueryJSONModel. Each query's JSON already contains parameters like direction, step, and queryType. This is the most idiomatic approach for per-query configuration.
Change backend.QueryDataHandler in grafana-plugin-sdk-go. This is the most disruptive option — it requires updating every datasource plugin in the Grafana ecosystem.

downstream_query_pipeline: api.DataQuery (api.go) — the actual HTTP call to Loki

existing_streaming_infrastructure.description: Loki already implements backend.StreamHandler with WebSocket-based streaming via /loki/api/v2alpha/tail. This is gated behind the 'lokiExperimentalStreaming' feature flag.
